samples.summary: A panel_digest that NO replicate records renders as "disagrees across replicates — see below", with nothing below — a false statement on every legacy report
samples.evidence: `reviewerFigures` sets `panelDigest = agreed.panel_digest && agreed.panel_digest !== NOT_STATED ? agreed.panel_digest : null` (report.mjs:1702). When every leg's `runJson.panel_digest` is absent — which is EVERY run written before this change, and the exact case the `not-recorded` state was designed for — all legs produce the same `NOT_STATED` value, so `agreed.panel_digest === NOT_STATED`, no entry is pushed into `disagreements`, and `panel_digest` is null. `renderReviewer` (report.mjs:1894-1898) then emits `| panel contents | **disagrees across replicates — see below** |` while the disagreement table below is empty (it is only rendered when `d.disagreements.length > 0`, line 1909). The same page's header row prints `panel_digest not-recorded` (line 1847), so the report contradicts itself and tells the reader the replicates are not one reviewer when they agree. `panel_sha` shares the code shape but is unreachable in that state because `buildReport` refuses an absent panel_sha; `panel_digest` has no such refusal. The rendered-absence case needs its own wording (e.g. "not recorded by any replicate").

samples.summary: score-all hands an envelope-READ digest down via --panel-digest, so every cross-run score it files records panel_digest_source "reconstructed" instead of "envelopes"
samples.evidence: `panelFlags` pushes `--panel-digest <digest>` whenever `isPanelDigest(panelDigest)` (score-all.mjs ~621), and `panel` came from `resolvePanelDigest({records: store.panelDigestRecords(ids)})` (score-all.mjs:724), i.e. it was READ off the runs' envelopes. In the child, `report.mjs`'s `resolvePanel` treats any `--panel-digest` as operator-asserted and returns `source: "reconstructed"` (report.mjs:3376), which `withPanelStamp` writes into the payload as `panel_digest_source`. So for every run that DOES record a digest — i.e. all runs written after this change, the normal CI lane at .github/workflows/eval-score.yml:199 — the filed score claims the digest was asserted after the fact rather than observed, and the child even prints `! panel_digest ... was STATED on the command line, not read from the runs`. That is exactly the attribution distinction `PANEL_DIGEST_SOURCES` and `validateScorePanel` exist to preserve, inverted on the default path. Nothing catches it: `validateScorePanel` only checks membership in the vocabulary.

samples.summary: All `mixed` pools collapse to one directory segment `__mixed__`, so a second cross-run score over a DIFFERENT panel mixture silently overwrites the first
samples.evidence: `panelKeySegment` maps every mixed resolution to the literal segment `mixed` (store.mjs, `PANEL_DIGEST_STATES.includes(value) → return value`), so `byConfigSegment(configHash, "mixed", corpusVersion)` yields one directory for any mixture under a given config+corpus. Scoring runs {A,B} and later runs {A,C} (same config_hash, same corpus_version, both with --allow-mixed-panel) writes both to `scores/by-config/sha256-…__mixed__<corpus>/<scorer>.json`, and `putScore` is deliberately re-writable, so the second overwrites the first with no diagnostic — the same overwrite-across-reviewers defect the third key segment was added to remove, reintroduced for pooled panels. `reports/…__mixed__….md` collides identically (score-all.mjs:559). `validateScorePanel` records `panel_digests` in the payload but does not prevent the collision. Keying on a hash of the sorted tally would keep distinct mixtures distinct.

samples.summary: On the render path the panel is resolved before the run-existence check, so a mistyped run id yields "a cross-run score must name the records it pools" instead of naming the missing run
samples.evidence: `const key = {..., panelDigest: resolvePanel(runIds).digest, ...}` at report.mjs:3450 runs before the loop at 3464-3476 that checks `store.getRun(runId) !== null`. `panelDigestRecords` silently skips run ids that do not exist (store.mjs:1074), so when all named runs are missing the record list is empty and `resolvePanelDigest` throws `a cross-run score must name the records it pools — with none, 'they all ran the same panel' is unfalsifiable`, which is caught only by `main().catch` and printed as `report failed: …`. The accurate message (`run "X" does not exist under this root`) is never reached. Moving the resolution below the existence loop fixes it.

samples.summary: panelDigestRecords is documented as a degrading read path but throws through getItem on an unreadable/corrupt item envelope
samples.evidence: The docblock says "A READ PATH, so it degrades: a run id that does not exist contributes no records rather than throwing", but the item loop calls `this.getItem(runId, itemId)` (store.mjs:1077), and `getItem` `refuse()`s on an unparseable `envelope.json` or `payload.json` (store.mjs:1039/1043/1049). Because panel resolution now runs on the render path, the persist path and the score-all preflight, one corrupt item envelope now aborts scoring/rendering of the whole comparison from a helper whose contract says it degrades. `listItems` filters incomplete items, so only the corrupt-JSON case reaches it — hence medium confidence, but the stated contract and the code disagree.

samples.summary: An operator --panel-digest is never checked against what the runs actually recorded, so it silently files scores under a panel that did not produce them
samples.evidence: score-all.mjs:721-724: `--panel-digest` is validated only for shape (`isPanelDigest`) and then short-circuits resolution entirely (`panelDigestArg ?? resolvePanelDigest(...)`), and the same is true in report.mjs:3370-3376. When the named runs DO record a digest and it differs from the stated one, nothing compares the two: the scores land under the stated panel, stamped `reconstructed`, and the mixed-panel refusal is bypassed as well (a pool of 5 panels can be filed as one panel by stating any digest). The flag is documented as being for runs that recorded none; refusing when the runs record a conflicting digest would keep the guard intact for the case it matters.

samples.summary: run.mjs's resolvePanelDigest destructures its argument with no `= {}` default, so a no-argument call is a TypeError rather than a refusal
samples.evidence: `export function resolvePanelDigest({ panelScript, override, digestOf = panelDigestOf })` — unlike the neighbouring `resolvePanelSha({ panelScript, override, git = gitLines })` pattern used elsewhere in this directory and unlike `readPanelFiles({...} = {})` in panel-identity.mjs, there is no `= {}`, so `resolvePanelDigest()` throws `Cannot destructure property 'panelScript' of 'undefined'` instead of the module's own refusal message. Also `path.resolve(panelScript)` is compared against `path.resolve(DEFAULT_PANEL_SCRIPT)` without `realpath`, so a symlinked-but-identical panel path is refused.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. When no replicate envelope records `panel_digest`, `stated()` (report.mjs:1558) maps each leg to NOT_STATED, so the axis at report.mjs:1661 agrees (distinct.length===1, line 1668-1670) and no disagreement entry is created; line 1702 then nulls `panelDigest` because it equals NOT_STATED, and line 1721 returns `panel_digest: null`. renderReviewer's ternary at report.mjs:1894-1898 therefore prints "| panel contents | **disagrees across replicates — see below** |" while the disagreement table (gated at line 1909) renders nothing and the else-branch at 1921-1929 simultaneously asserts the replicates are draws from one reviewer — a self-contradicting, factually false line. The path is reachable and unguarded: the CLI collects envelopes at report.mjs:3463-3476 and passes them to buildReport/reviewerFigures (3509-3516), and runs recording no digest are explicitly tolerated as the named state `not-recorded` with only a stderr warning (report.mjs:3381-3386; panel-identity.mjs:102-110), which is the exact case for every envelope written before the field existed. buildReport's refusal (report.mjs:1755-1759) applies only to the panelSha argument, not to the per-envelope panel_digest axis, so it does not guard this. Tests cover only the present case (report.test.mjs:2393) and a genuine disagreement (2455), leaving this state untested. Real, reachable, wrong-output logic bug in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `panelKeySegment` (store.mjs:377-387) passes any member of `PANEL_DIGEST_STATES` through unchanged, and `PANEL_DIGEST_MIXED = "mixed"` (panel-identity.mjs:111-112), so every mixture collapses to one segment. `byConfigSegment` (store.mjs:411-416) therefore yields a single directory `sha256-…__mixed__<corpus>` for any mixture under a given config+corpus, and `_scorePath` uses it for all cross-run scores (store.mjs:1156) while `putScore` deliberately overwrites (store.mjs:1160, SCORES_DIR docblock store.mjs:111-128). The path is reachable from the CLI: `resolvePanelDigest(..., allowMixed)` returns `mixed` for any multi-panel pool (panel-identity.mjs:470-477) and that value is used as the key at score-all.mjs:724 and report.mjs:3378 under `--allow-mixed-panel` (score-all.mjs:879/895). `validateScorePanel` (store.mjs:474-503) only requires the payload to say `mixed` and list ≥2 digests; it does not compare against any already-filed mixture, so scoring {A,B} and later {A,C} silently replaces the first score with no diagnostic. The report file collides the same way (score-all.mjs:551/559). No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable, and silent overwrite/data loss is in the correctness lane, so I cannot refute on any named ground.
